Date, year, week conversion

Chi Zhang

2022-05-04

Source: vignettes/date_conversion.Rmd
date_conversion.Rmd

These functions simplify work with dates and times across different formats.

Inputs can be numeric (e.g. 3) or character (e.g. "03", "2020-03"). The function suffix controls the output type: functions ending in _c return a character, those ending in _n return a double.

library(cstime)
#> cstime 2026.8.20
#> https://niphr.github.io/cstime/
library(magrittr)

Which year and week is this date?

With no arguments, these functions return the ISO year or ISO week of today.

date_to_isoyear_c()
#> [1] "2026"
date_to_isoyear_n()
#> [1] 2026
date_to_isoweek_c()
#> [1] "34"
date_to_isoweek_n()
#> [1] 34
# provide a date
date_to_isoyear_c('2021-01-01')
#> [1] "2020"
date_to_isoyear_n('2021-01-01')
#> [1] 2020
date_to_isoweek_c('2021-01-01')
#> [1] "53"
date_to_isoweek_n('2021-01-01')
#> [1] 53
date_to_isoyearweek_c('2021-08-11')
#> [1] "2021-32"

Get ISO year and ISO week from an ISO yearweek string 

isoyearweek_to_isoyear_c("2021-02")
#> [1] "2021"
isoyearweek_to_isoyear_n("2021-02")
#> [1] 2021
isoyearweek_to_isoweek_c("2021-02")
#> [1] "02"
isoyearweek_to_isoweek_n("2021-02")
#> [1] 2

The built-in dataset dates_by_isoyearweek is a reference table. Subset it to specific ISO years like this:

yrwk_19_20 <- dates_by_isoyearweek[isoyear %in% c(2019, 2020)]
head(yrwk_19_20)
